`src/diff.js` renders a unified diff between two texts, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public exports, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`.

This task is a completion exercise: every file and function in this workspace already holds its final implementation except `tokenize` in `src/diff.js`, whose body currently throws 'not implemented'. Implement only that function's body so it fulfills the specification above; keep its signature exactly as given, and do not edit any other file, export, or function. header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

1: /**
2:  * Line diff with unified output.
3:  *
4:  * Texts are compared line by line with a longest-common-subsequence walk;
5:  * output follows the unified diff format: two file headers, then one hunk per
6:  * changed region with up to `context` unchanged lines on each side.
7:  *
8:  * A line carries whether it ended with a newline, so the last line of a file
9:  * that does not end with one never matches the same text terminated normally.
10:  */
11: 
12: /** Marker printed after a line that is the end of a file without a newline. */
13: const NO_NEWLINE = '\\ No newline at end of file';
14: 
15: /**
16:  * Splits a text into lines and reports whether it ended with a newline.
17:  * @param {string} text Text to split.
18:  * @returns {{lines: string[], newlineAtEnd: boolean}} Lines without their terminators.
19:  * @throws {TypeError} When the text is not a string.
20:  */
21: export function splitLines(text) {
22:   if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TypeError('text must be a string');
23:   if (text === '') return { lines: [], newlineAtEnd: true };
24:   const newlineAtEnd = text.endsWith('\n');
25:   const body = newlineAtEnd ? text.slice(0, -1) : text;
26:   return { lines: body.split('\n'), newlineAtEnd };
27: }
28: 
29: /**
30:  * Turns a split text into tokens that remember their terminator.
31:  * @param {{lines: string[], newlineAtEnd: boolean}} split Result of `splitLines`.
32:  * @returns {Array<{text: string, terminated: boolean}>} One token per line.
33:  */
34: function tokenize(split) {
35:   throw new Error('not implemented')
36: }
37: 
38: /**
39:  * Builds the suffix table of longest-common-subsequence lengths.
40:  * @param {unknown[]} before Old items.
41:  * @param {unknown[]} after New items.
42:  * @param {(a: unknown, b: unknown) => boolean} same Item equality.
43:  * @returns {number[][]} Table where cell `i,j` is the LCS length of the suffixes.
44:  */
45: function lcsTable(before, after, same) {
46:   const rows = before.length;
47:   const columns = after.length;
48:   const table = Array.from({ length: rows + 1 }, () => new Array(columns + 1).fill(0));
49:   for (let i = rows - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
50:     for (let j = columns - 1; j >= 0; j -= 1) {
51:       table[i][j] = same(before[i], after[j])
52:         ? table[i + 1][j + 1] + 1
53:         : Math.max(table[i + 1][j], table[i][j + 1]);
54:     }
55:   }
56:   return table;
57: }
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Diffs two sequences.
61:  *
62:  * Where a deletion and an insertion are equally good, the deletion is emitted
63:  * first, so a replaced item reads as `-old` then `+new`.
64:  * @param {unknown[]} before Old items.
65:  * @param {unknown[]} after New items.
66:  * @param {(a: unknown, b: unknown) => boolean} same Item equality.
67:  * @returns {Array<{type: 'equal' | 'delete' | 'insert', item: unknown}>} Operations in file order.
68:  */
69: function diffSequence(before, after, same) {
70:   const table = lcsTable(before, after, same);
71:   const ops = [];
72:   let i = 0;
73:   let j = 0;
74:   while (i < before.length && j < after.length) {
75:     if (same(before[i], after[j])) {
76:       ops.push({ type: 'equal', item: before[i] });
77:       i += 1;
78:       j += 1;
79:     } else if (table[i + 1][j] >= table[i][j + 1]) {
80:       ops.push({ type: 'delete', item: before[i] });
81:       i += 1;
82:     } else {
83:       ops.push({ type: 'insert', item: after[j] });
84:       j += 1;
85:     }
86:   }
87:   while (i < before.length) {
88:     ops.push({ type: 'delete', item: before[i] });
89:     i += 1;
90:   }
91:   while (j < after.length) {
92:     ops.push({ type: 'insert', item: after[j] });
93:     j += 1;
94:   }
95:   return ops;
96: }
97: 
98: /**
99:  * Diffs two line arrays, comparing line text alone.
100:  * @param {string[]} before Old lines.
101:  * @param {string[]} after New lines.
102:  * @returns {Array<{type: 'equal' | 'delete' | 'insert', line: string}>} Operations in file order.
103:  * @throws {TypeError} When either argument is not an array of strings.
104:  */
105: export function diffLines(before, after) {
106:   checkLines(before);
107:   checkLines(after);
108:   return diffSequence(before, after, (a, b) => a === b).map((op) => ({ type: op.type, line: op.item }));
109: }
110: 
111: /**
112:  * Counts added, removed, and unchanged lines between two texts.
113:  * @param {string} oldText Text before the change.
114:  * @param {string} newText Text after the change.
115:  * @returns {{added: number, removed: number, unchanged: number}} Line counts.
116:  */
117: export function diffStats(oldText, newText) {
118:   const ops = diffLines(splitLines(oldText).lines, splitLines(newText).lines);
119:   const stats = { added: 0, removed: 0, unchanged: 0 };
120:   for (const op of ops) {
121:     if (op.type === 'insert') stats.added += 1;
122:     else if (op.type === 'delete') stats.removed += 1;
123:     else stats.unchanged += 1;
124:   }
125:   return stats;
126: }
127: 
128: /**
129:  * Groups the changed operations into hunks, each padded with context.
130:  *
131:  * Two changed regions separated by at most `2 * context` unchanged lines share
132:  * one hunk, since their context windows would otherwise overlap or touch.
133:  * @param {Array<{type: string}>} ops Operations to group.
134:  * @param {number} context Context lines on each side.
135:  * @returns {Array<{start: number, end: number}>} Inclusive operation ranges.
136:  */
137: function groupHunks(ops, context) {
138:   const changed = [];
139:   ops.forEach((op, index) => {
140:     if (op.type !== 'equal') changed.push(index);
141:   });
142:   if (changed.length === 0) return [];
143:   const runs = [];
144:   let start = changed[0];
145:   let end = changed[0];
146:   for (const index of changed.slice(1)) {
147:     if (index - end <= context * 2 + 1) {
148:       end = index;
149:     } else {
150:       runs.push([start, end]);
151:       start = index;
152:       end = index;
153:     }
154:   }
155:   runs.push([start, end]);
156:   return runs.map(([from, to]) => ({
157:     start: Math.max(0, from - context),
158:     end: Math.min(ops.length - 1, to + context),
159:   }));

goal.objective:
`src/diff.js` renders a unified diff between two texts, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public exports, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.

Do not add dependencies, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the tests' inputs; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`.
